datasets.name: Adaptive recruitment of cortex-wide recurrence for visual object recognition (EEG)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 34 participants (one session each) who viewed 242 object images, 121 challenge and 121 control images, selected from comparisons between human behavioural performance and AlexNet. The study examines adaptive recruitment of cortex-wide recurrent processing during visual object recognition. The derivatives folder contains outputs of the decoding analyses, including time-resolved decoding accuracy matrices for object identity (.npz).
datasets.authors: [Unspecified1], [Unspecified2]

datasets.name: iEEG_comprehensive_HFA_model_part2
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings acquired during non-REM sleep from patients undergoing invasive monitoring. It is part 2 of a comprehensive high-frequency activity (HFA) model study and supports analysis of sleep-related intracranial neural activity.
datasets.authors: Keisuke Hatano, Naoto Kuroda, Hiroshi Uda, Kazuki Sakakura, Michael J. Cools, Aimee F. Luat, Shin-Ichiro Osawa, Hitoshi Nemoto, Kazushi Ukishiro, Hidenori Endo, Nobukazu Nakasato, Yutaro Takayama, Keiya Iijima, Masaki Iwasaki, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: iEEG_comprehensive_HFA_model_part3
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings acquired during non-REM sleep from patients undergoing clinical monitoring. It is part 3 of a series supporting a comprehensive high-frequency activity (HFA) model, and the data underlie the associated Hatano et al. study (in press).
datasets.authors: Keisuke Hatano, Naoto Kuroda, Hiroshi Uda, Kazuki Sakakura, Michael J. Cools, Aimee F. Luat, Shin-Ichiro Osawa, Hitoshi Nemoto, Kazushi Ukishiro, Hidenori Endo, Nobukazu Nakasato, Yutaro Takayama, Keiya Iijima, Masaki Iwasaki, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: iEEG_comprehensive_HFA_model_part1
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings acquired during non-REM sleep, collected to support the development of a comprehensive model of high-frequency activity (HFA). It accompanies a forthcoming publication by Hatano and colleagues. Data were recorded at institutions in the United States and Japan.
datasets.authors: Keisuke Hatano, Naoto Kuroda, Hiroshi Uda, Kazuki Sakakura, Michael J. Cools, Aimee F. Luat, Shin-Ichiro Osawa, Hitoshi Nemoto, Kazushi Ukishiro, Hidenori Endo, Nobukazu Nakasato, Yutaro Takayama, Keiya Iijima, Masaki Iwasaki, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: SUBEMOcondEEG1
datasets.description: EEG, pupillometry, and behavioral data from 28 healthy adults performing an auditory fear conditioning paradigm with voice stimuli. Participants localized voices (left or right) across Pre-Conditioning, Conditioning, and Extinction phases, with conditioned voices paired with an aversive loud white noise using 50% partial reinforcement. The dataset supports research on emotional learning and auditory threat processing.
datasets.authors: Martina T. Cinca-Tomás, Judith Domínguez-Borràs

datasets.name: RNS_Epilepsy-iBIDS
datasets.description: A long-term intracranial EEG (iEEG) dataset from 8 epilepsy patients implanted with a responsive neurostimulation (RNS) system, recorded from bilateral epileptic lesion areas. Each recording contains 90 seconds of dual-channel iEEG around each stimulation, with stimulation markers and clinician-set stimulation parameters provided. The dataset supports study of changes in seizure onset patterns over the course of epilepsy and of iEEG changes following electrical stimulation.
datasets.authors: Chen Feng, Haoqi Ni, Zhoule Zhu, Hongjie Jiang, Zhe Zheng, Wenjie Ming, Shuang Wang, Kedi Xu, Junming Zhu

datasets.name: Passive but accessible:  Studied information is not actively stored in working memory, yet attended regardless of anticipated load
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a visual working memory experiment testing whether previously studied (learned) object information is actively held in working memory and whether it is attended regardless of anticipated memory load. Participants memorized lateralized objects that were either studied or novel, followed by a second screen of additional items whose appearance probability manipulated expected load, and then reported a probed object's color on a continuous color wheel.
datasets.authors: Yakup Yılmaz, Nursena Ataseven Özdemir, Wouter Kruijne, Elkan Akyürek, Eren Günseli
datasets.eeg_reference: Average of left and right mastoids (TP9/TP10); implemented by subtracting TP10/2 after initial left-mastoid reference.

datasets.name: Silent Visual Reading EEG
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw EEG recordings, in BrainVision format and organized according to BIDS, from participants silently reading word-by-word naturalistic narratives. It accompanies a study of auditory representations of words evoked during silent visual reading. Derivatives include preprocessed word-level EEG epochs, story and run metadata, expected/unexpected epoch labels, and corresponding feature embeddings.
datasets.authors: Jiawei Li, Adrien Doerig, Radoslaw Martin Cichy

datasets.name: Auditory Cortex Macaque Monkey DISC Data
datasets.description: Electrophysiological recordings from the auditory cortex of macaque monkeys, contributed by Kajikawa and Schroeder. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and mirrored on NEMAR from its original OpenNeuro deposit (ds007028).
datasets.authors: Yoshinao Kajikawa, Charles Schroeder

datasets.name: EEG Mortality Dataset in Parkinson's Disease
datasets.description: De-identified resting-state (eyes open) EEG recordings from individuals with Parkinson's disease and age-matched healthy controls. Each participant is labeled as living or deceased, so the data can be used to test whether resting EEG distinguishes later mortality. The dataset supports exploration of EEG biomarkers of mortality risk and development of machine learning classifiers.
datasets.authors: Simin Jamshidi, Arturo Espinoza, Soura Dasgupta, Nandakumar Narayanan

datasets.name: FOODEEG: An open dataset of human electroencephalographic and behavioural responses to food images
datasets.description: FOODEEG is an open dataset of electroencephalographic (EEG) and behavioural responses to food images from 117 participants. In one session, EEG was recorded during a food categorisation task in which participants judged images as healthy, tasty, or something they were willing to eat. In a second session, participants completed a food go/no-go task, a paired choice task, and questionnaires on dietary style and motivation. The dataset also includes raw and cleaned EEG data and normative ratings of the food stimuli from online samples.
datasets.authors: Chae, Violet, Grootswagers, Tijl, Bode, Stefan, Feuerriegel, Daniel

datasets.name: VR-Compassion Cultivation Training
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings collected during a virtual reality augmentation of compassion cultivation training (VR-CCT). Participants moved through a social world called Compassion Island, built in AltspaceVR, with a meditation hall, a garden courtyard and a clinic. They took part in guided meditation and compassion visualization exercises, and conversed with live-actor-animated avatars, including a guide and an agitated patient.
datasets.authors: Ying Wu, Enrique Carrillosulub, Leon Lange, Chloe Tanega, Nicole Wells, Erik Virre, Cassandra Vieten

datasets.name: Examining Perceptual Grouping on Stages of Processing in Visual Working Memory: An ERP Study
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 53 participants (N=39 used for stimulus-locked ERP analyses) performing a bilateral change-detection task to study how perceptual grouping by color repetition affects visual working memory (VWM). The design isolates neural correlates of individuation encoding, maintenance, initial comparison, percept-memory comparison, and late decision-making using the N2pc, CDA, N2, and FN400 ERP components. Conditions varied the number of items, color repetition, and spatial proximity of repeated items.
datasets.authors: Hanane Ramzaoui, Melissa Beck
datasets.eeg_reference: CMS (Common Mode Sense) and DRL (Driven Right Leg) passive electrodes

datasets.name: Motor Control Processes Moderate Visual Working Memory Gating Dataset
datasets.description: Raw (unpreprocessed) EEG recordings and behavioral data from 32 participants performing a visuomotor delayed match-to-sample task with interference. The study examined how motor control processes moderate visual working memory gating. Conditions crossed motor versus visuomotor interference with same versus different hand responses, alongside baseline trials with no interference.
datasets.authors: Şahcan Özdemir, Eren Günseli, Daniel Schneider

datasets.name: Dataset of Electroencephalograms of Juvenile Offenders
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from 140 Colombian young people: 74 juvenile offenders and 66 non-offender controls. Data were acquired with a 128-channel Biosemi ActiveTwo system. The dataset provides epoched and preprocessed EEG, along with spectral band-power features (delta, theta, alpha, beta) for eyes-open and eyes-closed epochs. It is intended to support the study of neurocognition in juvenile delinquency.
datasets.authors: Aura Polo, Elmer León-Becerra, Mariana Pino, Julie Viloria-Porto, Elmer León, Mariana Pino-Melgarejo

datasets.name: High Density Resting State EEG of Phantom Limb Pain and Controls
datasets.description: Resting state high-density EEG (64 or 128 channels) recorded from amputees with phantom limb pain, amputees without phantom limb pain, and intact pain-free controls. Recordings last approximately 7 minutes and were acquired with eyes open or eyes closed, as indicated by task. The data are organised according to the BIDS standard and include session-level pain questionnaire phenotype data.
datasets.authors: Ramne, M., Damercheli, S., Apelgren, F., Pettersson, I., Lendaro, E.
datasets.eeg_reference: Average, or channel A1 placed on left ear

datasets.name: Visual Naming EC
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 110 individuals performing a visual naming task. Electrode coordinates are provided in MNI-305 space, and events mark stimulus onset and response onset. The data were used in an analysis of whole-brain, millisecond-scale effective connectivity atlases of speech.
datasets.authors: Ryuzaburo Kochi, Aya Kanno, Hiroshi Uda, Keisuke Hatano, Masaki Sonoda, Hidenori Endo, Michael Cools, Robert Rothermel, Aimee F. Luat, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: Auditory Naming EC
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 121 individuals performing an auditory naming task. Electrode coordinates are provided in MNI-305 space, and each EDF file carries event markers for stimulus onset, stimulus offset, and response onset. The data were used in an analysis of whole-brain, millisecond-scale effective connectivity atlases of speech.
datasets.authors: Ryuzaburo Kochi, Aya Kanno, Hiroshi Uda, Keisuke Hatano, Masaki Sonoda, Hidenori Endo, Michael Cools, Robert Rothermel, Aimee F. Luat, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: No effect of rhythmic visual stimulation on experimental pain perception
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 41 participants who took part in a study of whether rhythmic visual stimulation modulates experimental pain perception. Data were collected at Université Laval, Québec, Canada. Pilot participants were excluded, so participant numbering starts at 12.
datasets.authors: Roy, N., Coll, MP, Coll LAB

datasets.name: Longitudinal Multitask Wireless ECoG Data from Two Fully Implanted Macaca fuscata
datasets.description: A longitudinal wireless subdural electrocorticography (ECoG) dataset recorded from two fully implanted Japanese macaques (Macaca fuscata). Recordings were acquired several times per week using an inductively powered wireless implant across multiple tasks, including rest, pressing, reaching, listening, and sensory evoked potentials. The data are organized according to the iEEG-BIDS specification to support reproducible neuroscience research.
datasets.authors: Huixiang Yang, Ryohei Fukuma, Tomoyuki Namima, Kotaro Okuda, Asaya Nishi, Takamitsu Iwata, Abdi Reza, Kota S Sasaki, Taro Kaiju, Gurlal Gill, Haruhiko Kishima, Shinji Nishimoto, Takufumi Yanagisawa

datasets.name: Discrepancy between self-report and neurophysiological markers of socio-affective responses in lonely individuals
datasets.description: EEG and behavioral data from 148 neurologically healthy adults performing an emotion processing and regulation task with static social and non-social images. Participants passively watched neutral or negative images or reappraised negative ones, then rated arousal and valence. The dataset supports examination of discrepancies between self-reported and neurophysiological markers of socio-affective responses in lonely individuals.
datasets.authors: Szymon Mąka, Marta Chrustowicz, Łukasz Okruszek

datasets.name: Targeted Neuromodulation of the Left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex Alleviates Altered Affective Response Evaluation in Lonely Individuals
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG and behavioral recordings from 120 healthy adults performing an emotion processing and regulation task with static images under sham and active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Each participant completed two counterbalanced sessions. It includes preprocessed ERP derivatives and tDCS side-effect and blinding-effectiveness questionnaire data, and examines affective response evaluation in lonely individuals.
datasets.authors: Szymon Mąka, Marta Chrustowicz, Łukasz Okruszek

datasets.name: Urban Appraisal: Physiological Recording during Rating of Different Urban Environments
datasets.description: This dataset contains continuous EEG, ECG and electrodermal activity (EDA) recordings from 63 participants who viewed and rated Streetview images of different urban environments on a desktop PC. It was collected to investigate how urban environments and their elements influence urban appraisals and neural responses, including stimulus-onset ERPs (P1, N1, P3, LPP). Each participant rated 56 images on nine subjective scales, and semantic segmentation of the images provides predictors for subjective and neural responses.
datasets.authors: Carolina Zaehme, Isabelle Sander, Klaus Gramann

datasets.name: AlphaDirection1: EEG, ECG, PPG in the resting state and working memory for sequentially and simultaneously presented digits
datasets.description: Raw 64-channel EEG, ECG, PPG and behavioral recordings from 30 healthy young adults (18–32 years) during resting state and a verbal working memory digit-span task with serial recall. The resting session alternated eyes-closed and eyes-open blocks followed by passive cartoon viewing. In the working memory task, seven-digit sequences were presented visually either simultaneously or sequentially at different rates and with different inter-stimulus intervals, allowing study of how presentation mode affects neural oscillations and peripheral physiology.
datasets.authors: Alexandra I. Kosachenko, Danil I. Syttykov, Dmitry A. Tarasov, Alexander I. Kotyusov, Yuri G. Pavlov

datasets.name: IACKD: Intention Action Conflict EEG-Hand Kinematics Dataset
datasets.description: IACKD is an EEG and hand kinematics dataset designed to study conflict between motor intention and executed action. It pairs EEG recordings with hand movement kinematics, and is organized in BIDS format with BrainVision EEG files. Task presentation was implemented in PsychoPy.
datasets.authors: Mengpu Cai, Rongrong Fu, Yaodong Wang, Bin Lu, Saiwei Guo, Fangyao Xu

datasets.name: EEG recordings during sham neurofeedback in virtual reality
datasets.description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recordings acquired during a sham neurofeedback experiment in a virtual reality environment. The study examined how feedback valence (positive, negative, or none) modulates alpha-band activity during an attentional task. Each participant completed positive, negative, control, and resting-state (eyes open/eyes closed) conditions.
datasets.authors: C. Brigitte Aguilar Gonzales, Collaborators from the Experimental and Computational Neuroscience Group

datasets.name: Visual Attribute-Specific Contextual Trajectory Paradigm 2.0
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw neuroimaging recordings collected with the Visual Attribute-Specific Contextual Trajectory Paradigm 2.0. The paradigm is used to study how the brain generates domain-general visual surprise signals and how their latency depends on the visual attribute that is violated. It accompanies a pre-print on attribute-dependent latency of visual surprise signals.
datasets.authors: Benjamin Lowe (ben.lowe@mq.edu.au), Naohide Yamamoto (naohide.yamamoto@qut.edu.au), Jonathan Robinson (jonathan.robinson@monash.edu), Patrick Johnston (dr.pat.johnston@icloud.com)

datasets.name: NeuroTechs Dataset for Stem Skills
datasets.description: An EEG dataset from the NeuroTechs group, collected in the context of STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) skills. Recordings were acquired with a Unicorn wearable EEG system through its Python API, and values are provided in microvolts. The dataset is organized according to BIDS with HED annotations.
datasets.authors: Tania Yareni Pech-Canul, Roberto Guajardo, Luis Fernando Acosta-Soto, Mónica Sofía Margoya-Constantino, Juan Pablo Rosado-Aíza, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi

datasets.name: Collaborative rule learning promotes interbrain information alignment
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 24 pairs of participants performing a 4-way categorisation task based on rules they first agreed upon together. Participants also completed pre- and post-tests on the same stimuli. The data were collected to investigate how collaborative rule learning promotes information alignment between interacting brains.
datasets.authors: Moerel, Denise, Grootswagers, Tijl, Quek, Genevieve L., Smit, Sophie, Varlet, Manuel

datasets.name: Resting-state EEG before and after different study methods
datasets.description: Open-access resting-state EEG recordings from 21 neurotypical undergraduate students at the Federal University of Paraíba, Brazil, collected before and after different study methods. Participants were randomly assigned to an active learning group (retrieval practice with feedback), a passive learning group (review of lecture notes), or a control group with no review. The dataset supports research in cognitive neuroscience, educational neuroscience, and the neural correlates of learning and memory.
datasets.authors: Paloma Victoria de Sales Alves, Antonio Simeão Sobrinho Neto, Carla Alexandra da Silva Moita Minervino

datasets.name: Multiple Object Monitoring (EEG)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 30 participants performing a Multiple Object Monitoring (MOM) task, in which observers sustain attention to moving stimuli. The recordings were collected to investigate whether EEG can detect lapses in sustained attention. The data are organized according to the BIDS standard.
datasets.authors: Benjamin G. Lowe, Alexandra Woolgar, Sophie Smit, Anina N. Rich

datasets.name: Neural decoding of competitive decision-making in Rock-Paper-Scissors
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings from 62 participants, organized into 31 pairs, who played a computerised version of the competitive Rock-Paper-Scissors game across 480 games. It was collected to study the neural correlates of competitive decision-making and to support decoding of choices and outcomes from brain activity. Each session lasted about one hour.
datasets.authors: Moerel, Denise, Grootswagers, Tijl, Chin, Jessica L.L., Ciardo, Francesca, Nijhuis, Patti, Quek, Genevieve L., Smit, Sophie, Varlet, Manuel

datasets.name: Chimeric music reveals an interaction of pitch and time in electrophysiological signatures of music encoding
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 27 normal-hearing adults listening to original monophonic music and 'chimeric' music, in which the pitch contours and note onset times of two melodies are exchanged. This distorts musical pattern while preserving the marginal pitch and timing statistics. The dataset supports investigation of pitch-time interactions in the electrophysiological encoding of music. It includes a click-train phase and a music phase with 33 trials per stimulus type.
datasets.authors: Tong Shan, Edmund C. Lalor, Ross K. Maddox

datasets.name: Alpha power indexes working memory load for durations
datasets.description: Raw magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 23 healthy adults performing an n-item delayed temporal reproduction task. Participants held sequences of one or three empty auditory intervals in memory and then reproduced them by button press. The dataset also includes EOG, ECG, digitized head and electrode positions, a two-minute eyes-open resting-state recording, and individual anatomical MRI. It supports research on working memory dynamics, auditory processing, motor responses and resting activity.
datasets.authors: Sophie K. Herbst [1], Izem Mangione [1], Charbel-Raphaël Segerie [2], Richard Höchenberger [2], Tadeusz Kononowicz [1, 3, 4], Alexandre Gramfort [2], Virginie van Wassenhove [1], [1] Cognitive Neuroimaging Unit, INSERM, CEA, Université Paris-Saclay, NeuroSpin, 91191 Gif/Yvette, France [2] Inria, CEA, Université Paris-Saclay, Palaiseau, France [3] Institute of Psychology, The Polish Academy of Sciences, ul. Jaracza 1, 00-378 Warsaw, Poland [4] Institut NeuroPSI - UMR9197 CNRS Université Paris-Saclay

datasets.name: Validation of Sleep Staging with Forehead EEG Patch
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from a three-electrode forehead patch (CGX) used to validate automated spectral sleep staging against manually scored standard 33-channel polysomnography. Files include manual visual hypnograms in 30-second epochs and spectral sleep staging results for each patch channel. The 33-channel polysomnography data are not part of this release and will be published separately.
datasets.authors: Julie Onton, Sarah Mednick

datasets.name: Poetry Assessment EEG Dataset 1
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings and behavioural ratings from participants who read and evaluated 210 short English-language texts: 70 Haiku, 70 Senryu, and 70 non-poetic control texts. Each text was rated on aesthetic appeal, vivid imagery, being moved, originality, and creativity. This first of two BIDS datasets includes 47 participants whose recordings passed technical validation. Psychometric questionnaire data and resting-state EEG are also provided.
datasets.authors: Soma Chaudhuri, Joydeep Bhattacharya

datasets.name: Poetry Assessment EEG Dataset 2
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings and behavioural ratings from four participants who read and evaluated 210 short English-language texts: Haiku, Senryu, and non-poetic control texts. Each text was rated on aesthetic appeal, vivid imagery, being moved, originality, and creativity. These participants' recordings were acquired in segments because of session interruptions and were concatenated during preprocessing. They are released as a companion to the main Poetry Assessment EEG Dataset 1 for completeness and transparency.
datasets.authors: Soma Chaudhuri, Joydeep Bhattacharya

datasets.name: SINGSING
datasets.description: SINGSING is a simultaneous EEG and MEG dataset from twenty adult participants who listened to harmonic complex sounds that varied in frequency in an auditory oddball paradigm. It supports investigation of pre-attentive pitch processing at sensor and source levels, and allows comparison of EEG and MEG recordings acquired at the same time.
datasets.authors: Valerie Chanoine, Jean-Michel Badier, Mireille Besson, Talya Inbar

datasets.name: cBCI Matrix Multimodal Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous EEG and eye-tracking recordings from 21 healthy participants performing a matrix-based single-character-presentation BCI spelling task. Calibration and copy-spelling sessions include event markers for target and non-target stimuli. It supports research on multimodal sensor fusion for EEG-based brain-computer interface typing systems.
datasets.authors: Basak Celik, Tab Memmott, Matthew Lawhead, Srikar Ananthoju, Deniz Erdogmus

datasets.name: The role of REM sleep in neural differentiation of memories in the hippocampus
datasets.description: This dataset contains fMRI and EEG recordings from 69 participants examining the role of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep in the neural differentiation of memories in the hippocampus. Each participant completed three fMRI scans and one EEG session, which contained either nap sleep data or quiet wake data depending on the participant's condition.
datasets.authors: Elizabeth A. McDevitt, Ghootae Kim, Nicholas B. Turk-Browne, Kenneth A. Norman

datasets.name: Dimension-based attention modulates early visual processing
datasets.description: Continuous 64-channel scalp EEG from 12 observers performing a visual dimension-based attention (cue) task, originally reported by Gramann, Töllner and Müller (2010). The recordings, 56-66 minutes each, include ICA decomposition weights and expert-annotated independent component labels. The dataset was later used to study automatic multi-class labeling of ICA components and is known as the "Cue" dataset.
datasets.authors: Klaus Gramann, Thomas Töllner, Hermann J. Müller

datasets.name: Social Observation EEG raw data
datasets.description: Raw EEG recordings from a social observation study, curated in BIDS format with HED annotations. The README is an unfilled template, so detailed information on the participants, task and experimental design is not provided. The dataset is a NEMAR-hosted copy of OpenNeuro dataset ds006554.
datasets.authors: Yaner Su

datasets.name: Visual EEG Study (BrainVision → BIDS)
datasets.description: This dataset contains high-density EEG recordings collected during a visual stimulation task. Data were converted from BrainVision format (.vhdr/.vmrk/.eeg) to the EEG-BIDS specification, with a single session per participant. No acquisition-time filters or offline preprocessing are included.
datasets.authors: Sanaz Ghaffari, Arian Yavari, Sara Bonyadian, Arsalan Ghofrani, Russell Butler

datasets.name: Resting EEG
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recorded with a 128-channel EGI system from participants who also underwent structural MRI. The dataset was first reported in a study of whole-brain electrophysiological functional connectivity dynamics in resting-state EEG. Data were preprocessed with band-pass and notch filtering, artifact and bad-channel handling, average re-referencing, and downsampling to 250 Hz.
datasets.authors: Computational Neuroimaging and Neuroengineering Lab ar the University of Oklahoma

datasets.name: Dataset of intracranial EEG during cortical stimulations evoking negative motor responses
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) recordings acquired during 41 high-frequency electrical cortical stimulations that evoked negative motor responses. Data come from 23 patients undergoing presurgical evaluation for drug-resistant epilepsy. Each recording spans about 24 seconds around a stimulation and includes pre- and post-stimulation 5-second epochs, which were used for connectivity analysis. Stimulation contact pairs, current intensities and evoked effects are annotated in the events files.
datasets.authors: Andrei Barborica, Cristina Ghita, Laurentiu Tofan, Irina Oane, Ioana Mindruta

datasets.name: Skill learning and consolidation in healthy humans
datasets.description: A longitudinal MEG dataset investigating brain activity during early skill learning, overnight consolidation, and longer-term retention in 31 healthy right-handed adults. Participants performed a sequential finger tapping task with the non-dominant left hand across up to three MEG sessions (initial training, about 24 hours later, and about 30 days later), with resting-state scans before and after practice. Anatomical MRI, behavioral responses, eye tracking and pupillometry, and forearm EMG were also recorded and synchronized with MEG.
datasets.authors: Bönstrup, M, Buch, ER, Cohen, LG

datasets.name: Young Adult Resting State and Auditory Oddball Task EEG Data
datasets.description: Resting-state and auditory oddball task EEG recordings from young adults, collected under two conditions: a control condition and an arousal condition induced by threat of unpredictable shock. Recordings include eyes-open and eyes-closed rest, plus passive and active auditory oddball tasks with standard, target, and distractor tones. The dataset supports investigation of arousal and locus coeruleus-noradrenaline system related neural activity.
datasets.authors: Andy Jeesu Kim, Mara Mather, Santiago Morales, Joshua Senior

datasets.name: MEG-SCANS - A comprehensive magnetoencephalography speech dataset with Stories, Chirps And Noisy Sentences.
datasets.description: MEG-SCANS provides raw and MaxFiltered magnetoencephalography recordings from 24 German-speaking participants who listened to about one hour of auditory stimuli. The stimuli were two audiobooks, 120 Oldenburg Matrix Sentence Test (OLSA) sentences at varying intelligibility levels, and short up-chirps for signal quality assessment. The dataset also includes empty-room recordings, structural MRI, audiograms, speech reception threshold results, and audio stimulus material. It is organized in BIDS and intended as a benchmark for encoding and decoding analyses of brain responses to speech.
datasets.authors: Till Habersetzer, Bernd T. Meyer

datasets.name: 3M-CPSEED：An EEG-based Dataset for Chinese Pinyin Production in Overt, Silent-intended, and Imagined Speech
datasets.description: 3M-CPSEED is an EEG dataset recorded from 20 healthy native Chinese speakers performing Chinese Pinyin production in overt, silent-intended, and imagined speech conditions. The stimulus set of selected finals and initials covers key articulatory features of the Chinese phonological system. The dataset supports research on speech neurophysiology, neural differences across pinyin articulations, and transfer learning to other alphabetic languages.
datasets.authors: Xinyu Ma, Jiang Yi, Ning Jiang

datasets.name: LIGHT Hypnotherapy
datasets.description: EEG and ECG recordings collected during guided imagery hypnotherapy (LIGHT) sessions, in which a hypnotherapist uses storytelling and deep visualization to promote personal growth and well-being. The approach targets eudaemonic well-being, emphasizing meaning and self-realization, which distinguishes it from traditional hypnotherapy. The dataset includes a baseline resting EEG session and in-lab recordings from selected hypnotherapy sessions.
datasets.authors: anonymous

datasets.name: The auditory brainstem response to natural speech is not affected by selective attention
datasets.description: EEG recordings from three experiments investigating whether selective attention to natural speech modulates the auditory brainstem response and cortical responses. Experiments 1 and 2 used diotic and dichotic presentation of two competing audiobooks with attention directed to one narrator, while Experiment 3 used passive listening to audiobook stimuli from a previous study. Simultaneous cortical (32-channel active) and subcortical (bipolar passive, with eardrum electrodes in a subset of participants) recordings are provided in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Thomas J Stoll, Nathan D Vandjelovic, Melissa J Polonenko, Nadja R S Li, Adrian K C Lee, Ross K Maddox

datasets.name: Electrophysiological markers of surprise-induced failures of visual and auditory awareness
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 33 participants who each completed both a visual and an auditory surprise task, with task order counterbalanced. The dataset supports investigation of electrophysiological markers of surprise-induced failures of visual and auditory awareness. Data from participants excluded at various analysis stages are included up to the stage of processing they reached.
datasets.authors: En-Lin Leong, Yun Da Chua, Takashi Obana, Christopher L. Asplund

datasets.name: HED schema library for SCORE annotations example
datasets.description: A BIDS example dataset demonstrating annotation of intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings with the HED schema library for SCORE (Standardized Computer-based Organized Reporting of EEG). It contains iEEG data from one subject recorded during clinical photic stimulation at Mayo Clinic. Events are annotated through an events.tsv column whose levels are defined as HED tags in the events.json sidecar, yielding machine-readable annotations validated with the BIDS and HED validators.
datasets.authors: Tal Pal Attia, Kay Robbins, Dora Hermes

datasets.name: PhysioMotion_Artifact
datasets.description: PhysioMotion_Artifact is an EEG dataset organized in BIDS format, apparently intended to characterize physiological and motion-related artifacts in electroencephalographic recordings. It is distributed via OpenNeuro and NEMAR. The README provides little detail about the participants or recording protocol.
datasets.authors: Jiangwei Yu, Aonan He

datasets.name: Expectation effects on repetition suppression in nociception
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings collected to study how expectation affects repetition suppression in nociception. It supports investigation of how the brain's responses to repeated painful stimuli are modulated by predictions about those stimuli. The data are organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Lisa-Marie Pohle, Moritz Nickel, Birgit Nierula, Markus Ploner, Ulrike Horn, Falk Eippert

datasets.name: Memory Reactivation Levels Remain Unaffected by Anticipated Interference Experiment 2 Dataset
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a visual working memory experiment (Experiment 2) examining whether memory reactivation levels are affected by anticipated interference. Participants memorized 2 or 6 lateral objects, then performed either a dual task with distractors or a single fixation-only task during the delay, before selecting the cued object in a probe display. The data have been preprocessed; the preprocessing steps are described in the associated preprint and OSF repository (Experiment 2).
datasets.authors: X

datasets.name: Mouse Sleep Staging Validation dataset (MSSV)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG and EMG recordings with expert sleep scores from 92 healthy mice, collected across five laboratories in Italy, Denmark, Switzerland, and France. It includes recordings from both light and dark phases and is intended for validating automated mouse sleep staging methods across labs.
datasets.authors: Laura Rose, Alexander Neergaard Zahid, Javier García Ciudad, Christine Egebjerg, Louise Piilgaard, Frederikke Lynge Sørensen, Mie Andersen, Tessa Radovanovic, Anastasia Tsopanidou, Maiken Nedergaard, Sébastien Arthaud, Renato Maciel, Christelle Peyron, Chiara Berteotti, Viviana Lo Martire, Alessandro Silvani, Giovanna Zoccoli, Micaela Borsa, Antoine Adamantidis, Morten Mørup, Birgitte Rahbek Kornum

datasets.name: Neocortical and Hippocampal Theta Oscillations Track Audiovisual Integration and Replay of Speech Memories
datasets.description: Raw MEG dataset with T1-weighted anatomical scans and behavioural logfiles from an audiovisual speech memory experiment. Participants completed repeated blocks of encoding (audiovisual synchrony detection on speech movies), a distractor task, and cued retrieval of the auditory speech associated with a speaker's face. The data support analyses of neocortical and hippocampal theta oscillations in audiovisual integration and memory replay.
datasets.authors: Biau E, Wang D, Park H, Jensen O, Hanslmayr S

datasets.name: Chisco-2.0
datasets.description: Chisco-2.0 is an EEG dataset of imagined speech recorded from two participants (sub-01 and sub-02). The raw recordings are provided in EDF format and organized according to the BIDS standard. The dataset is intended to support research on decoding imagined speech from brain activity.
datasets.authors: Zihan Zhang, Yu Bao, Tianyi Jiang, Xiao Ding, Xia Liang, Juntong Du, Yi Zhao, Kai Xiong, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

datasets.name: Tethered EEG Recordings in Syngap1 rats
datasets.description: Six-hour tethered EEG recordings from wildtype and Syngap+/Δ-GAP heterozygous rats (male, 12-16 weeks old), collected between zeitgeber times 3 and 9 under a 12:12 light-dark cycle. Recordings used a head-mounted 32-channel EEG array with accelerometers, sampled at 1 kHz. Most animals have two recording sessions. The data support study of SYNGAP1-related neurodevelopmental pathophysiology.
datasets.authors: Lucy Pritchard, Ingrid Buller-Peralta, Sally M Till, Peter C Kind, Alfredo Gonzalez-Sulser

datasets.name: Dataset of psychophysiological data from children with learning difficulties who strengthen reading and math skills through assistive technology
datasets.description: This dataset contains psychometric and EEG data from 76 Mexican children with reading or math learning difficulties. Children were assigned to an experimental group, who used the online learning method Smartick for three months, or a control group with no intervention. EEG (resting state and reading or arithmetic tasks) and psychometric assessments were collected before and after the intervention to evaluate gains in reading and math skills.
datasets.authors: César E. Corona-González, Claudia Rebeca De Stefano-Ramos, Juan Pablo Rosado-Aíza, David I. Ibarra-Zarate, Fabiola R. Gómez-Velázquez, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi

datasets.name: MetaRDK
datasets.description: MetaRDK contains intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) high-gamma activity from patients with pharmacologically intractable epilepsy performing a perceptual random-dot motion decision task followed by a confidence judgement. The data comprise average power modulation in five non-overlapping frequency bands between 70 and 150 Hz, segmented from trial onset to trial offset and sampled at 512 Hz. Behavioral tables (stimulus onset, response times, confidence, changes of mind) accompany the recordings to study the neural correlates of decision making and metacognition.
datasets.authors: Dorian Goueytes, Francois Stockart, Alexis Robin, Lucien Gyger, Martin Rouy, Dominique Hoffmann, Lorella Minotti, Philippe Kahane, Michael Pereira, Nathan Faivre

datasets.name: Picture naming
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 108 individuals performing a picture-naming task. Electrode coordinates are provided in MNI-305 space, and events mark stimulus onset and response onset. The data were used to study early facilitative and late compensatory neural interactions underlying naming.
datasets.authors: Ryuzaburo Kochi, Aya Kanno, Hiroshi Uda, Keisuke Hatano, Hidenori Endo, Michael Cools, Robert Rothermel, Aimee F. Luat, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: MultisensoryFlickerHealthyYoungAdults_AllSubjectsRawData
datasets.description: Scalp EEG recordings from healthy young adults during one hour of sensory stimulation. Conditions were 40 Hz audiovisual (multisensory) flicker, a no-flicker control, or randomized flicker as sham stimulation. Participants performed a psychomotor vigilance task throughout the sessions. The dataset contains raw data for all subjects.
datasets.authors: Matthew Attokaren, Annabelle Singer

datasets.name: EEG data during three near-threshold visual detection tasks: a no-cue task, a noninformative cue task (50% validity), and an informative cue task (100% validity)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants performing three near-threshold visual detection tasks that differed in cue information: a no-cue task, a noninformative cue task (50% validity), and an informative cue task (100% validity). The dataset was collected to study how prestimulus alpha-band activity relates to perception of near-threshold visual stimuli. It is shared in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: María Melcón, Enrique Stern, Lydia Arana, Almudena Capilla

datasets.name: Essex EEG Movie Memory dataset
datasets.description: Raw EEG recordings from 27 participants who watched 10-second clips extracted from movies they had previously seen. For each clip, participants reported whether they recognised the movie and whether they remembered watching it before. When a clip was recognised or remembered, it was shown a second time and participants marked the moments that prompted recognition with a mouse click. The dataset supports research on memory and recognition of naturalistic video stimuli.
datasets.authors: Ana Matran-Fernandez, Sebastian Halder

datasets.name: OWM-Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains processed intracranial EEG recordings from frontal (middle frontal gyrus) and temporal (middle temporal gyrus) areas of 13 epilepsy patients performing a load-3 object working memory task. Trials are 6498 ms long (fixation, encoding, and delay periods) and include only those retained after artifact rejection. Per-subject trial indexes and behavioral performance tables are provided as source data.
datasets.authors: Vladimir Omelyusik, Tyler S. Davis, Satish S. Nair, Behrad Noudoost, Patrick Hackett, Elliot H. Smith, Shervin Rahimpour, John D. Rolston, Bornali Kundu

datasets.name: iEEG_Neural_spatial_volatility
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) dataset titled 'Neural spatial volatility', collected by Kuroda, Asano, Nakasato and colleagues, with ethics approval from the IRBs of Wayne State University and Tohoku University. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and mirrored on NEMAR from its original OpenNeuro deposit (ds006107).
datasets.authors: Naoto Kuroda, Eishi Asano, Nobukazu Nakasato

datasets.name: EEG dataset for speech decoding
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from phoneme discrimination tasks combined with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of the motor cortex. It merges two studies: a 2019 study of consonant-vowel and vowel-consonant pairs in 8 participants, and a 2021 study in 16 participants that added single phonemes, real words and pseudowords. It is intended to support research on speech decoding and the role of articulation and coarticulation in speech perception.
datasets.authors: João Pedro Carvalho Moreira, Vinícius Rezende Carvalho, Eduardo Mazoni Andrade Marçal Mendes, Ariah Fallah, Terrence J. Sejnowski, Claudia Lainscsek, Lindy Comstock

datasets.name: Mind in Motion Older Adults Walking Over Uneven Terrain
datasets.description: This dataset contains high-density, dual-layer EEG recorded together with neck EMG, inertial measurement unit acceleration, and ground reaction force from older adults walking over uneven terrain at different speeds. Each participant completed two three-minute trials per walking condition plus a three-minute seated rest trial. Digitized electrode locations are provided for each subject.
datasets.authors: Chang Liu, Erika M. Pliner, Jacob S. Salminen, Ryan Downey, Jungyun Hwang, Akraprava Roy, Ryland Swearinger, Natalie Richer, Chris J. Hass, David J. Clark, Todd M. Manini, Yenisel Cruz-Almeida, Rachael D. Seidler, Daniel P. Ferris

datasets.name: TSS_iEEG
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 7 participants undergoing closed-loop, theta-synchronized stimulation of human hippocampal networks. The dataset accompanies a study showing that closed-loop control of theta oscillations enhances hippocampal network connectivity. Recordings are segmented into pre- and post-stimulation evoked potentials, pre- and post-stimulation rest, closed-loop stimulation, and control stimulation periods.
datasets.authors: James Kragel, Joel Voss

datasets.name: Sustained Attention Task (gradCPT) Dataset using simultaneous EEG-fMRI and DTI
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings, diffusion-weighted imaging, and behavioral data from 28 healthy adults performing a gradual-onset continuous performance task (gradCPT) that probes sustained attention. Resting-state (eyes open and closed), 15 Hz checkerboard, and imagery tasks are also included. Raw data and preprocessed derivatives are provided.
datasets.authors: Younghwa Cha, Yeji Lee, Eunhee Ji, SoHyun Han, Sunhyun Min, Hyoungkyu Kim, Minseo Cho, Hae Seong Lee, Youngjai Park, Joon-Young Moon

datasets.name: A complementary dataset of open-eyes EEG recordings in a photo-stimulation setting from: Alzheimer's disease, Frontotemporal dementia and Healthy subjects
datasets.description: This dataset provides eyes-open scalp EEG recordings acquired during intermittent photic stimulation (5 to 30 Hz in 5 Hz steps) from 36 participants with Alzheimer's disease, 23 with frontotemporal dementia, and 29 healthy controls. It complements an earlier eyes-closed resting-state dataset of the same cohort, and participant numbers match between the two. Raw and preprocessed (filtered, ASR- and ICA-cleaned) recordings are provided in BIDS format alongside clinical MMSE scores and demographics.
datasets.authors: Aimilia Ntetska, Andreas Miltiadous, Alexandros T. Tzallas, Katerina D. Tzimourta, Theodora Afrantou, Panagiotis Ioannidis, Dimitrios G. Tsalikakis, Nikolaos Grigoriadis, Pantelis Angelidis, Konstantinos Sakkas, Emmanouil D. Oikonomou, Nikolaos Giannakeas, Markos G. Tsipouras

datasets.name: somatomotor
datasets.description: A multi-modal neuroimaging dataset combining structural MRI (T1w), magnetoencephalography (MEG), and EEG recorded during electrical median nerve stimulation at the right wrist. Participants responded to each stimulus by lifting the left index finger as quickly as possible, allowing study of somatosensory and motor responses. Anatomical fiducials were digitized to align MEG with MRI, and event triggers mark stimuli and finger-lift responses.
datasets.authors: Fa-Hsuan Lin, Deirdre Foxe von Pechmann, Kaisu Lankinen, Seppo Ahlfors, Bruce Rosen, Jyrki Ahveninen, Matti Hämäläinen, Tommi Raij

datasets.name: Synchronous EEG and fMRI dataset on inner speech
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous EEG and fMRI recordings from participants performing an inner speech task, in which eight words were presented in random order and repeated across trials. Data were acquired with a 3T MRI scanner and a 64-channel BrainProducts EEG system in three subjects across two sessions each. EEG data include pulse artifact removal and are organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Foteini Simistira Liwicki

datasets.name: Cognitive Electrophysiology in Socioeconomic Context in Adulthood: An EEG dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 127 young adults (18-30 years) together with retrospective indicators of childhood family socioeconomic status (SES) and adult SES measures, including education, income, food security, and home and neighborhood characteristics. EEG was recorded during ERP CORE tasks or adaptations of them, which target perception, cognition, and action. The dataset also includes an adult ADHD symptoms checklist, so that links between SES, ADHD symptoms, and neural activity can be examined in a socioeconomically diverse sample.
datasets.authors: Elif Isbell, Amanda N. Peters, Dylan M. Richardson, Nancy E. R. De León

datasets.name: A geometric shape regularity effect in the human brain: MEG dataset
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 20 adult participants viewing simple geometric shapes such as hexagons, triangles and quadrilaterals. The dataset supports a study of how the human brain encodes geometric regularity, including symmetries and parallelism, and contrasts it with visual processing in convolutional neural networks and transformer models. It is released anonymized and defaced in BIDS format, alongside a companion fMRI dataset.
datasets.authors: Mathias Sablé-Meyer, Lucas Benjamin, Cassandra Potier Watkins, Chenxi He, Maxence Pajot, Théo Morfoisse, Fosca Al Roumi, Stanislas Dehaene

datasets.name: General Info: inst-comp-eeg
datasets.description: EEG dataset from an instruction-following study in which participants received novel verbal instructions combining integration or selection of animate and inanimate images, a relevant feature (color or shape), and a response key. Each participant completed a main instruction-following task and a 1-back localizer task in a single session. The dataset supports investigation of neural representations of novel instructions.
datasets.authors: Pena, P., Palenciano, A.F., González-García, C., Ruz, M.

datasets.name: iEEG_visual
datasets.description: This dataset contains electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from two human participants viewing visual stimuli, including high-contrast vertical gratings and noise patterns with different spatial frequencies and spectral power distributions. Participants fixated on a central dot that changed color at random times. The data were used to study stimulus dependence of gamma oscillations and the relationship between neuronal synchrony, BOLD response, and the local field potential in human visual cortex.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Winawer, Dora Hermes

datasets.name: ERC_CoG PROMENADE - WP2 - MetaImagery (Metaphor and Mental Imagery)
datasets.description: EEG and behavioral dataset from 39 Italian-speaking university students performing a picture-matching task in which target pictures matched or mismatched a preceding cue. Cues were physical (picture), imagery (single word), literal sentence, or metaphorical sentence. The data are provided as preprocessed long epochs (filtered, mastoid re-referenced, ocular ICA cleaned). The dataset was collected within the ERC PROMENADE project to test how mental representations generated by different cue types influence target picture processing. Vocabulary and mental imagery measures are included per participant.
datasets.authors: Federico Frau, Paolo Canal, Maddalena Bressler, Chiara Pompei, Valentina Bambini
datasets.eeg_reference: online reference: FCz; offline reference: average mastoids

datasets.name: PWIe
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a picture-word interference (PWI) picture-naming experiment conducted at the NeuroCognition Laboratory at San Diego State University. Participants named line drawings preceded by English distractor words that were semantically related, identical in name, or unrelated to the picture, while EEG and verbal responses were recorded. The dataset supports investigation of the neural correlates of lexical access and semantic interference during speech production.
datasets.authors: Phillip J. Holcomb, Jacklyn Jardel, Katherine J. Midgley, and Karen Emmorey

datasets.name: Visuomotor_task
datasets.description: An intracranial EEG (iEEG) dataset recorded from ten epilepsy patients undergoing invasive monitoring for seizure localization. Participants played five sessions of Speed Match, a visuomotor game on the Lumosity platform, during interictal recording. Continuous iEEG recordings are provided in EDF format with channel information and event markers for finger tapping.
datasets.authors: Riyo Ueda, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: EEG: RL Task (3-Armed Bandit) with alcohol cues in hazardous drinkers and ctls
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a three-armed bandit reinforcement learning task in which alcohol-related and non-alcohol beverage cues were presented to 53 community participants, including hazardous drinkers and controls. The dataset supports investigation of electrophysiological markers of cue-specific exploration in hazardous drinking. This derivative version was processed with the NEMAR pipeline.
datasets.authors: Ethan Campbell, James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: Song Familiarity
datasets.description: EEG recordings from twenty-nine participants who listened to song melodies and responded as soon as a song felt familiar. Participants then tried to identify the song (title, artist, or lyrics) and chose the title from a four-option multiple choice display, receiving visual feedback on correctness. The dataset includes synchronized audio reconstructions of what each participant heard, supporting research on music familiarity and recognition.
datasets.authors: Jared R. Girard, Aaron M. Bishop, Cameron D. Hassall

datasets.name: SeizeIT2
datasets.description: SeizeIT2 is a multicenter, prospective dataset of wearable behind-the-ear EEG, ECG, EMG and movement recordings from 125 adult and pediatric patients with focal epilepsy. Patients were monitored in five European epilepsy monitoring units with the Sensor Dot wearable device alongside standard video-EEG. The dataset contains about 11,640 hours of wearable data with 886 recorded focal seizures, annotated in BIDS-score compatible format, and supports the development and validation of seizure detection algorithms.
datasets.authors: Miguel Bhagubai, Christos Chatzichristos, Lauren Swinnen, Jaiver Macea, Jingwei Zhang, Lieven Lagae, Katrien Jansen, Andreas Schulze-Bonhage, Francisco Sales, Benno Mahler, Yvonne Weber, Wim Van Paesschen, Maarten De Vos

datasets.name: EEGEyeNet Dataset
datasets.description: A BIDS-standardized example dataset of simultaneously recorded EEG and eye-tracking data from a single subject, drawn from the EEGEyeNet resource. EEGEyeNet was designed as a dataset and benchmark for eye movement prediction from EEG. This version reformats the original Open Science Framework data to the BIDS standard.
datasets.authors: Martyna Beata Płomecka, Ard Kastrati, Nicolas Langer

datasets.name: Flankers-FAR
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a visual word flanker task in which participants judged four-letter real words and pseudowords presented centrally, with no flankers, identical flankers, or different flankers. It was collected at the NeuroCognition Laboratory in San Diego to study orthographic processing and parafoveal flanker effects on word recognition. The dataset comprises 270 trials per participant with behavioral responses made via game controller.
datasets.authors: Brennan Terhune-Cotter, Phillip J. Holcomb, Katherine J. Midgley, Sofia E. Ortega, Emily M. Akers, Karen Emmorey

datasets.name: Flankers-NEAR
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a flanker paradigm with visually presented four-letter words and pseudowords. Targets appeared with no flankers, identical flankers, or different flankers, and participants judged each item as a real word or pseudoword using a game controller. Data were collected at the NeuroCognition Laboratory in San Diego across 270 trials per participant.
datasets.authors: Brennan Terhune-Cotter, Phillip J. Holcomb, Katherine J. Midgley, Sofia E. Ortega, Emily M. Akers, Karen Emmorey

datasets.name: Cognitive Electrophysiology in Socioeconomic Context in Adulthood
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 127 young adults (18-30 years) collected alongside retrospective objective and subjective measures of childhood family socioeconomic status (SES) and adult SES indicators, including educational attainment, income, food security, and home and neighborhood characteristics. Tasks were taken or adapted from the ERP CORE compendium to capture perception, cognition, and action-related neural activity. The dataset also includes an ADHD-related symptoms checklist, allowing analyses of links between SES, ADHD symptoms, and brain electrophysiology.
datasets.authors: Elif Isbell, Amanda N. Peters, Dylan M. Richardson, Nancy E. R. De León

datasets.name: ltpDelayRepFRReadOnly
datasets.description: ltpDelayRepFRReadOnly is an EEG dataset from Michael Kahana's laboratory, collected with a delayed, repeated-item free recall paradigm. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and distributed as a read-only release. It supports research on human episodic memory and the neural correlates of free recall.
datasets.authors: [Adam Broitman], [Michael Kahana]

datasets.name: NOD-EEG
datasets.description: NOD-EEG is an electroencephalography dataset of human responses to naturalistic ImageNet object images. It extends the Natural Object Dataset-fMRI (NOD-fMRI) by recording EEG, and MEG in a companion dataset, from the same subjects viewing the same stimuli. Together the three modalities support study of object recognition with both high spatial and high temporal resolution. The dataset includes raw BIDS data, preprocessed continuous data, epoched data, and detailed trial-level metadata.
datasets.authors: Guohao Zhang, Ming Zhou, Shuyi Zhen, Shaohua Tang, Zheng Li, Zonglei Zhen

datasets.name: NOD-MEG
datasets.description: NOD-MEG is a magnetoencephalography dataset of human subjects viewing naturalistic object images drawn from ImageNet. It extends the Natural Object Dataset-fMRI (NOD-fMRI) with MEG and EEG recorded from the same subjects viewing the same stimuli. Together the modalities offer high spatial and high temporal resolution for studying object recognition. The release includes raw BIDS data, preprocessed continuous data, epochs, and detailed trial-level event tables.
datasets.authors: Guohao Zhang, Ming Zhou, Shuyi Zhen, Shaohua Tang, Zheng Li, Zonglei Zhen

datasets.name: MULTI-CLARID (Multimodal Category Learning and Resting-state Imaging Data)
datasets.description: MULTI-CLARID is a combined fMRI/EEG dataset acquired during an auditory category learning task and resting state. It includes 63-channel EEG with ECG, EOG, facial EMG and skin conductance, plus respiration and finger-pulse recordings, and T1-weighted and UTE anatomical MR scans. Five participants' datasets containing the multi-dimensional category learning experiment are currently shared.
datasets.authors: Jörg Stadler, Torsten Stöter, Nicole Angenstein, Andreas Fügner, Marcel Lommerzheim, Artur Mathysiak, Anke Michalsky, Gabriele Schöps, Johann van der Meer, Susann Wolff, André Brechmann

datasets.name: SpinalExpect_NonInvasive
datasets.description: This dataset contains non-invasive electrophysiological recordings from the human cervical spinal cord in 30 healthy young adults, collected to test whether temporal expectation influences initial sensory processing in the spinal cord. Participants received electric median nerve stimulation at the left wrist after an auditory cue, with the cue-stimulus interval either fixed at 1100 ms or varied randomly between 100 and 2100 ms. Participants silently counted rare double-stimulus trials (80 ms ISI) and reported the count at the end of each block.
datasets.authors: Max-Philipp Stenner, Cindy Marquez Nossa, Tino Zaehle, Elena Azanon, Hans-Jochen Heinze, Matthias Deliano, Lars Buentjen

datasets.name: SpinalExpect_Invasive
datasets.description: Invasive epidural recordings from the cervical spinal cord of eight patients with neuropathic pain and implanted epidural electrodes, collected to test whether temporal expectation alters initial sensory processing in the human spinal cord. Participants received median nerve stimulation preceded by an auditory cue, with the cue-to-stimulus interval either fixed (1100 ms) or randomly varied (100-2100 ms) in alternating blocks. Participants silently counted rare double-stimulus trials (80 ms ISI).
datasets.authors: Max-Philipp Stenner, Cindy Marquez Nossa, Tino Zaehle, Elena Azanon, Hans-Jochen Heinze, Matthias Deliano, Lars Buentjen

datasets.name: visStim
datasets.description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from 20 C57BL/6 mice in three cohorts: blinking light only, transcranial diagnostic ultrasound (tDUS) only, and combined tDUS with light. The dataset was collected to test how tDUS modulates the visual cortex's response to external visual stimulation. It includes raw, event-triggered, and processed ECoG data.
datasets.authors: Henry Tan, Devon Griggs, Lucas Chen, Kahte Culevski, Kat Floerchinger, Alissa Phutirat, Gabe Koh, Nels Schimek, Pierre Mourad
datasets.placement_scheme: 1 channel in L+R visual cortices and L+R somatosensory cortices

datasets.name: PerceiveImagine
datasets.description: An EEG dataset of a perception and mental imagery task. Participants viewed an image for 6 seconds in response to an auditory prompt, then closed their eyes and imagined the same image for 6 seconds. A further prompt sound started the next trial. The recordings can be used to study neural correlates of visual perception versus imagery and to develop decoding methods.
datasets.authors: Li Zhiyuan, Zhao Jiaxin

datasets.name: SEEG Resting State Recording
datasets.description: This dataset contains resting-state stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from two patients with epilepsy, acquired with implanted depth electrodes. It is provided in BIDS format as raw intracranial EEG data.
datasets.authors: Prof. Pengfei Xu

datasets.name: Mapping object space dimensions: new insights from temporal dynamics
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw EEG data in BIDS format from participants viewing object images, collected to map the dimensions of object space and examine their temporal dynamics. Source data include trial-level behavioral event files detailing what was shown on screen during the EEG session. The dataset accompanies a study on how object representations unfold over time.
datasets.authors: Alexis Kidder(*), Genevieve Quek, Tijl Grootswagers

datasets.name: Color Change Detection Task
datasets.description: Raw electrophysiological recordings from a color change detection task, a visual working memory paradigm. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and is available through OpenNeuro and NEMAR. The README provides little detail on the participants or the acquisition, so the description is limited to what the dataset name and metadata state.
datasets.authors: [Unspecified]
